content: A Lab-on-Chip Impedance Flow Cytometer Utilizing a CMOS Electrode Array | EECS at UC Berkeley A Lab-on-Chip Impedance Flow Cytometer Utilizing a CMOS Electrode Array Venkata Alapati EECS Department, University of California, Berkeley Technical Report No. UCB/EECS-2025-181 December 1, 2025 http://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Pubs/TechRpts/2025/EECS-2025-181.pdf This report presents the development of a novel CMOS impedance ï¬ow cytometer as part of a progress towards developing a CMOS impedance deformability ï¬ow cytometer (SEMI- IDC) for rapid, label-free cellular analysis based on mechanical properties. By integrating innovations in semiconductor technology, microï¬uidics, and data science, our work aims to provide a low-cost, portable alternative to conventional ï¬ow cytometry systems, which often remain constrained by high costs, bulky instrumentation, and complex sample preparation requirements. The work begins with a review of existing literature to identify relevant design strategies and inform the system architecture. Practical considerations are then explored through simulations to validate theoretical assumptions and guide engineering decisions. The system is subsequently implemented and evaluated, demonstrating successful bead detection and preliminary classiï¬cation performance based on particle size. The results highlight the feasibility of utilizing CMOS electrodes in a handheld platform for basic impedance cytometry and establish a foundation for future improvements for the SEMI-IDC platform. Ongoing work focuses on enhancing classiï¬cation accuracy via improving the ï¬uidic pump system, extending device longevity by protecting the sensing electrodes, and expanding the deviceâs performance capabilities by more aggressive time measurements. The vision is to one day help rapidly identify and treat various pathological diseases like cancer, sepsis, and blood disorders.
